question: How much does representing each observed MLE search-tree fragment as all root-to-leaf trajectories duplicate shared-prefix edges and change the implicit task and physical-run weights relative to one-row-per-observed-edge representation?

population.rows: all eligible endpoints in the fixed snapshot blind manifests
population.observed_edge: child to parent only when both endpoint identities occur in the same fixed blind population
population.fragment_root: an endpoint whose declared parent is absent from the fixed blind population
population.fragment_leaf: an endpoint with no observed child in the fixed blind population
population.unique_edge_representation: each observed child-parent edge has weight one
population.branch_linearized_representation: enumerate every fragment-root-to-fragment-leaf path; an observed edge receives multiplicity equal to its number of descendant fragment leaves
population.single_node_fragments: counted structurally but contribute zero edges in both representations

classification_rule: Gate failure takes precedence. Otherwise MULTI_AXIS requires the duplicate-fraction, task-TV, and run-TV thresholds; RUN_LEVEL requires the duplicate-fraction and run-TV thresholds; any positive duplicate count below those gates maps to DUPLICATION_WITHOUT_MATERIAL_WEIGHT_SHIFT; exact zero duplication maps to NO_OBSERVED_LINEARIZATION_DUPLICATION.

claim_boundary.allowed_if_multi_axis: On this fixed outcome-blind MLE-agent snapshot, root-to-leaf linearization materially duplicates shared-prefix edges and changes both task and physical-run empirical weights under the predeclared thresholds.
claim_boundary.allowed_if_run_level: On this fixed outcome-blind MLE-agent snapshot, root-to-leaf linearization materially duplicates shared-prefix edges and changes physical-run empirical weights under the predeclared thresholds; task-mix materiality is not supported.

failure_rule: Any snapshot, hash, schema, graph, support, security, byte-reproducibility, or independent-verification mismatch fails closed without changing the population, fragment rule, weighting rule, threshold, or classification order.
